Question: What is a dirty cache line in a write-back cache?

Question: Reasoning question 8: What is the role of a write buffer?
Option1: Compile the firmware
Option2: Replace the instruction decoder
Option4: Temporarily hold pending writes so the processor can continue in some cases
CorrectAnswer: Temporarily hold pending writes so the processor can continue in some cases

Question: Concept check 8: What is a dirty cache line in a write-back cache?
Option1: A line modified in cache but not yet written back to lower memory
Option2: A line with no valid data
Option3: A line that contains only zeros
Option4: A line that has never been accessed
CorrectAnswer: A line modified in cache but not yet written back to lower memory
Explanation: Dirty indicates the cached copy differs from the lower-level copy.

Question: Applied scenario 8: What is a cache allocation policy on a write miss concerned with?
Option1: Whether a missed write causes a block to be brought into the cache
Option2: How the vector table is sorted
Option4: How an IRQ is named
CorrectAnswer: Whether a missed write causes a block to be brought into the cache
Explanation: Allocation policy determines whether to allocate a cache line after a write miss.

Question: Design review 8: What is one purpose of a cache line replacement policy?
Option1: Guarantee that all memory accesses hit
Option2: Eliminate the memory hierarchy
Option3: Reduce future misses by selecting a suitable victim line
Option4: Change the CPU instruction set
CorrectAnswer: Reduce future misses by selecting a suitable victim line
Explanation: Replacement decisions affect which blocks remain available for future accesses.

Question: Debugging scenario 8: What does a fully associative cache allow?
Option1: Each block has exactly one possible cache line
Option2: A memory block can be placed in any cache line
Option3: Every set contains only one line
Option4: No memory block can be cached
CorrectAnswer: A memory block can be placed in any cache line
Explanation: Fully associative placement has no fixed set restriction for a block.

Question: Exam practice 8: What is direct-mapped cache organization?
Option1: Each set contains every cache line
Option2: Each memory block maps to exactly one cache line
Option3: Each block can be placed anywhere in the cache
Option4: A cache with no tags
CorrectAnswer: Each memory block maps to exactly one cache line
Explanation: Direct mapping assigns each memory block to one line based on its index.

Explanation: The tag distinguishes memory blocks that map to the same cache location.
